title: Direction of motion
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the rod moves to the right, applying the left-hand rule for magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor.

title: Number of batteries
description: Essential: The final numerical answer for the number of lithium batteries must be 100.

title: Force equilibrium reasoning
description: Important: The solution must state that for constant velocity, the magnetic (Ampere) force equals the opposing mechanical resistance of 400 N.

title: Current calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly use F = BIL to calculate the required current (I = 400 A).

title: Voltage and Ohm's Law
description: Important: The solution must apply Ohm's Law (U = IR) to find the voltage (400 V) across the rod, recognizing the rod's resistance is the relevant load.

title: Series voltage summation
description: Optional: The response may explicitly note that the total source voltage is the sum of individual battery voltages (n * 4 V).

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The solution may demonstrate unit analysis for equations like F = BIL and U = IR.

title: Incorrect force direction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the left-hand rule is misapplied, leading to an incorrect direction (e.g., leftward motion).

title: Neglecting force equilibrium
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the constant velocity condition (net force = 0, so F_magnetic = F_resistance) is not stated or used.

title: Ohm's Law misapplication
description: Pitfall: Penalize if Ohm's Law is incorrectly applied (e.g., using total circuit resistance incorrectly or confusing EMF with terminal voltage).
